**Repaired finding submitted: compliant (at fallback) — no redline, no counterparty comment.**

What I changed in this pass:

- **Quote:** reverted to the clean, sentence-complete operative indemnity from p0090 ("Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless…"), which is the actual obligation the rule tests.
- **Evidence chain made explicit in the rationale** so the infringement element is verifiable without relying on the quote alone: the clause heading "13. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INDEMNITY" (p0087), the ownership/non-interference warranty that triggers the indemnity, the express infringement scenario in p0090, and the remedy ladder at p0091–p0093.
- **Documented the check limitation:** the indemnity verb and the word "infringement" are ~618 characters apart in p0090, so no single verbatim quote can carry both within the 600-character cap. This is why the "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present" heuristic fails on any permissible quote — a drafting/phrasing artefact (the trigger is breach of the non-infringement warranty rather than the words "infringement claim"), not a substantive gap.

Substance is unchanged and matches the verifier's own reading: the indemnity runs Vendor→Customer, covers settlement sums and legal fees, carries the standard procure/substitute/replace-or-modify remedies, and is expressly carved out of the Section 15 cap and consequential-damages exclusion (p0105) — better than the fallback's 3× super-cap. No reverse Sparkling indemnity exists, so walk-away does not arise.

Preferred-position shortfalls (no defend/control-of-defence mechanic, no refund remedy, IP-only scope, affiliates unnamed, ten-day notice) remain recorded as sub-elements for negotiation leverage rather than deviations, per the playbook's classification semantics.
